children: After a long wait, Claude developer Anthropic PBC
is finally a publicly traded company. The news is a positive for many firms across the AI and semiconductor industry, including chip giant Broadcom

. Not only does the move bolster Anthropic’s ability to make good on its large-scale commitments to Broadcom, but it also pushes back on one of the key concerns Broadcom’s CEO outlined earlier this year.
Anthropic Fortifies Balance Sheet With IPO and Private Placement Proceeds
Anthropic’s total chip leasing commitments to Broadcom are

params.linkText: $161.2 billion over the next five years

children: , excluding interest. With these commitments, Broadcom expects Anthropic to become its largest XPU customer in 2027, and to sustain that position in 2028. This makes Anthropic’s ability to pay Broadcom critical to the chip giant achieving its forecast for $350 billion in AI semiconductor sales from its fiscal year 2027 to fiscal year 2028.

Anthropic’s total commitments to AI hyperscalers and neoclouds are also several times larger than its commitment to Broadcom. To satisfy all these payments, getting its hands on as much cash as possible is key. Luckily for Anthropic and its suppliers, the company’s latest share offerings will significantly bolster its balance sheet.

Anthropic set its IPO price at $83 and initially offered 980 million shares. After removing the 23.6 million shares sold by certain stockholders, Anthropic listed proceeds from the original offering, after underwriting discounts but before other expenses, at around $78.8 billion. Underwriters subsequently exercised their option to buy 147 million additional shares, bringing the total offering to 1.127 billion shares and Anthropic's gross IPO proceeds to approximately $91.6 billion.

Separately, the company closed a private share placement worth around $26 billion, with Broadcom among the investors. Including this, Anthropic raised approximately $117.6 billion in gross proceeds from newly issued shares across both offerings, before fees and expenses.

The company’s amended S-1 filing shows that it was already in a very strong cash position, with cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of around $131.8 billion. Its final prospectus estimates that these holdings would have totaled approximately $244.6 billion on a pro forma adjusted basis as of Sept. 30, assuming the completed offerings and full exercise of the underwriters' option, after estimated expenses and related tax withholding obligations.

This massive piggy bank should go a long way toward helping Anthropic fund its lease and compute commitments over the coming years as it looks to increase its profitability. Although the company’s sales are growing rapidly and margins are improving, its commitments still dwarf the size of its profits. In the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic’s adjusted operating profit was $4.08 billion, and its operating cash flow was $6.57 billion.
Anthropic’s IPO Demand Signals Willingness to Commit Capital to AI Firms
When discussing constraints on the AI buildout going forward, Broadcom’s CEO Hock Tan

, “What I think might be the biggest constraint is capital.” In this context, the strong demand for Anthropic’s IPO is a positive sign, indicating that investors are still willing to commit capital to AI companies.

Around a week before going public, Anthropic said the expected price for its IPO was between $70 and $78 per share. The company also said it expected to offer 825 million shares. Based on these numbers, the high end of Anthropic’s gross proceeds from the offering
, including shares sold by existing stockholders.

However, reports soon emerged that the company’s IPO was around six times oversubscribed, indicating very strong investor demand. In turn, the company increased both the price per share and the number of shares offered, putting its IPO proceeds well above this previous figure.
Something similar has played out with the recent equity and bond offerings at Meta Platforms

. These offerings were all several times oversubscribed according to reports, again signaling strong demand to provide capital to AI companies. This is another positive sign for Broadcom, as Meta is also one of its top chip customers, with the companies partnering to design Meta’s custom AI accelerators.

Still, just because Anthropic and Meta are able to attract capital today doesn’t mean the entire AI ecosystem can, or that this will continue indefinitely. Pressure is already building on debt issuance in the form of higher interest rates and credit spreads, as shown by Meta’s recent offerings.
Wall Street Continues to Eye Strong Upside in Broadcom Shares

Anthropic’s IPO is another strong development for Broadcom’s outlook as the company targets immense AI chip sales growth over the coming years. Notably, Broadcom shares had recovered significantly since plummeting below $300 after markets reacted to the midterm election results. However, the stock took another big hit on Nov. 12, falling below $310.Wall Street analysts have generally maintained a bullish outlook on Broadcom. The MarketBeat consensus price target near $525 implies over 70% upside. However, Rothschild & Co Redburn significantly decreased their target in November from $595 to $398.

title: Anthropic's Record IPO Could Ease a Major Concern for Broadcom Investors
